chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Husayni narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Isa ibn Abi Maryam al-Ajali informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ziyad al-Azrami narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hatem al-Manqari narrated from Mufaddal ibn Umar, saying: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Path.

He said: It is the way to the knowledge of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and there are two Paths: a Path in this world, and a Path in the Hereafter. As for the Path that is in this world, it is the Imam whose obedience is obligatory; whoever knows him in this world and follows his guidance will pass over the Path that is the bridge of Hell in the Hereafter, and whoever does not know him in this world, his foot will slip from the Path in the Hereafter and he will fall into the Fire of Hell.

key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Path (Sirat), specifically referring to the bridge over Hell and the path to God
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: The Hereafter, the realm of eternal consequence
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The Imam, identified here as the manifestation of the Path in this world
key_terms.جِسْرُ جَهَنَّمَ: The Bridge of Hell, the eschatological path all must cross
key_terms.مَعْرِفَةُ اللَّهِ: Knowledge of God, the ultimate goal of the path
key_terms.مَفْتُرَضُ الطَّاعَةِ: Obligatory obedience, a key theological attribute of the Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Path (Sirat) in Shia theology according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the dual nature of 'As-Sirat' by identifying the worldly path as the Imam, whose recognition (*ma'rifah*) is the prerequisite for salvation. This establishes the Shia doctrine that obedience to the Imam is not merely ritualistic but the essential bridge (*jibr*) that ensures safe passage over the bridge of Hellfire in the Hereafter. The hadith underscores the inseparable link between earthly spiritual authority and eternal destiny, a core tenet of Shia eschatology.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Ahmad bin Hasan al-Qattan, that he said: We were told by Abdul-Rahman bin Muhammed al-Hussaini, that he said: We informed told by Abu Ja’far, Ahmad bin Isa bin Abi Maryam al-‘Ajali, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Ahmad bin Abdullah bin Ziyad al-‘Azrami, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Hatem al-Manqari, from Mufaddal bin Umar, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, about the Path.

So he said: It is the Way to conscious knowledge of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and they are two Paths: a Path in this world, and a Path in the Hereafter. As for the Path that is in this world, it is the Imam whose obedience is obligatory; the one who knows him in this world and follows his guidance, will walk on the Path that is the bridge of Hell in the Hereafter, and the one who does not know him in this world, his foot will slip off the Path in the Hereafter and collapse into the Fire of Hell.
